blocks.text: Intro
Wurlitzer tremolo, warm and close, light room ambience
Verse 1
Wurlitzer rhythmic chords, soft kick + brushed snare

We gather in a season of mourning
The kind that hurts as it heals
A quiet acknowledgment
Of a world that no longer feels

Step forward on shaky ground
Eyes on a thinning sun
Some will come with us
Some will refuse the run
Pre-Chorus
harmony voices enter, rhythm steadies

The rails are set
But not every car will stay
Steel screams loud
When the couplings give way
Chorus
gospel lift, but restrained and solemn

Dearly beloved
We rise and begin
The shining city
Is the light we carry within

Dearly beloved
The signal is clear
Radiate forward
The future starts here
Verse 2
groove deeper, upright bass enters

Some drag the chain behind them
Some swear their focus is true
But forward only belongs
To the ones who choose

No gatekeepers left now
No towers to defend
Just signal carried farther
Than any single friend
Pre-Chorus
choir thicker, organ enters

No magic waiting
No promised land
Just new foundations
Built by human hands
Chorus
fuller choir, drums stronger

Dearly beloved
We rise and begin
The shining city
Is the light we carry within

Dearly beloved
The signal is clear
Radiate forward
The future starts here
Bridge
instrumentation drops, spoken sermon tone

What do we become
When the dust finally clears?

What kind of world
Do we build from here?

Love in the music
Fire in the art
Respect in the words
And courage in the heart
Final Chorus
choir dominant, slow and powerful

Dearly beloved
We rise and begin
The shining city
Is the light we carry within

Dearly beloved
The call rings true
Radiate outward
The future is you

notebook.style: Mid-tempo soul-folk (~96 BPM), Wurlitzer electric piano provides the main rhythmic texture with warm tremolo chords, Drums play a restrained groove with kick and brushed snare, gradually opening into a fuller kit in later sections, Electric bass supports with simple melodic movement that reinforces the steady forward pulse, Subtle Hammond organ pad or light tremolo electric guitar widens the pre-chorus and chorus sections without dominating the mix, No choir or group vocals, Lead vocal delivery should feel grounded, reflective, and conversational, gradually building conviction rather than theatrical intensity, Production should feel analog and human—warm room ambience, slight grit, and the sense of a small band playing together in one space
